note: Programmatic input schemas for the fifteen interactive tools. Agents replicate each tool's logic by feeding these inputs to the documented formulas / shipped JS (assets/js/<id>.js); the UI pages are the human front-end for the same logic.

tools.title: Niche Picker
tools.description: Answer 6 questions, get ranked niche suggestions with reasoning — or take the 4-question "Pick my 2027 niche" branch.

q1.description: What you could talk about for 100 videos.

q3.description: Max money per view, biggest audience, or balance.

q271.description: 2027 branch: what's your 2027 bet (rising format / search demand / underserved lane / evergreen).

q273.description: 2027 branch: which risk you can stomach.

tools.output: Ranked niche list (top 3+) with per-niche reasoning and fit tags. The 2027 branch returns top-3 niches with trajectory badges, basis sentences, and risk notes.
tools.drive_notes: Scoring logic lives in assets/js/quiz.js: option tags are matched against each niche's fit[] tags, q3 sets an RPM preference filter, q6 sets the competition ceiling. The niche catalogue (9 niches, fit tags, rpm/competition levels) is embedded in quiz.js. The 2027 branch scores the 20 atlas niches against data/niches.json outlook_2027 trajectories (heating +3 / stable +1 / cooling -2), growth-signal matches, format fit, risk alignment, and atlas skill_fit — OUTLOOK_2027 in quiz.js mirrors the JSON and tests/niche-atlas.test.js checks sync.

tools.title: Revenue Calculator
tools.description: Project revenue from views, niche, sponsors, and affiliates — with honest ranges.

niche.description: Must be a key of calculators.json youtube_longform_rpm_bands.

avg_sponsor_video_views.description: Expected views on the sponsored video(s).

tools.output: Monthly revenue range [lo, hi] split into long-form ads, Shorts ads, sponsorships, affiliate/products, plus annualized totals. Ranges, never promises.
tools.drive_notes: Math (assets/js/calculator.js): long-form ads = views/1000 × RPM band from calculators.json; Shorts ads = shorts/1000 × shorts_rpm_per_1000; sponsorships = deals × (sponsor views/1000) × sponsorship_rule_of_thumb.dedicated_cpm_range; affiliate = input × 0.7–1.3.

tools.title: 90-Day Planner
tools.description: Generate a posting schedule from your platforms and cadence. Printable.

platforms.description: Where the shorts go (e.g. TikTok, Reels, Shorts).

rest_day.description: 0=Mon … 6=Sun; that day is rest + analytics review.

tools.output: 13-week posting schedule (91 days): per-day long-form and short-form assignments, totals, a day-45 checkpoint review note.
tools.drive_notes: Layout logic (assets/js/planner.js): long-form spread across non-rest days, shorts spread 2 days apart, week 7 flagged as the midpoint review. Rest day is non-negotiable — no posting, analytics review only.

tools.title: Sponsor Deal Analyzer
tools.description: Benchmark a sponsor offer against the 2026 rate card — verdict, red-flag checklist, counter-offer worksheet.

deliverable.description: Integrated slot, dedicated video, or short-form video.

expected_views.description: If known, enables the implied-CPM check.

tools.output: Verdict (UNDERPAID / FAIR / STRONG), benchmark range, implied CPM vs rate-card CPMs, red-flag checklist (usage, whitelisting, exclusivity, payment), counter-offer worksheet with line items.
tools.drive_notes: Logic (assets/js/deal-analyzer.js): followers → tier (nano/micro/macro/mega) → per_video_or_post_by_tier range for platform; verdict = offer vs range; counter starts at range top (creators list ~23% above what they accept) + usage line items (paid30 +50%, paid180 +75%, paid365 +100%) + exclusivity (30d +25%, 60–90d +50%). Negotiation aid, not financial advice.

tools.title: The Deal Room
tools.description: Manage the whole deal: track offers through signing, price usage rights, rehearse negotiations, export your memo.

expected_views.description: Last-10-video average; the number sponsors buy.

timeline.description: Due date / delivery window as written in the offer.

status.description: Where the deal sits in the offer → paid pipeline.

tools.output: Tracked deal records with rate-card verdicts (UNDERPAID / FAIR / STRONG + the ~23% listed-vs-accepted note), usage-rights line-item pricing (reported +50/+75/+100% band; no invented whitelisting/buyout multipliers), per-situation negotiation scripts, interactive red-flag checklist scoring, and a one-page deal memo.
tools.drive_notes: Logic (assets/js/deal-room.js, UMD — importable in node): scoreOffer(offer, lo, hi) benchmarks against sponsorship_rate_card_2026; priceUsage(baseFee, tierId, usage_rights_tiers) applies the reported multipliers, returning guidance instead of numbers for whitelisting/buyout; redFlagScore(checkedIds, red_flags) scores contract structure (any walk_away flag or 3+ points -> walk away); renderScript(script, vars) fills {{placeholders}}; dealMemo(deal, scored, flags) builds the one-page record. Scripts + checklist + tiers live in api/v1/deal-templates.json. Negotiation aid, not financial/legal/tax advice.

tools.title: Hiring Cost Calculator
tools.description: Price your first hire: monthly/annual cost and the ad revenue needed to cover it — honest math, no promises.

role.description: Video editor, thumbnail designer, virtual assistant, channel manager/ops.

billing_model.description: hourly = rate/hr × hours/week; per_video = rate × units/month; monthly = retainer.

monthly_views.description: Your current monthly long-form views, for the coverage math.

tools.output: Monthly/annual cost (sticker vs +15% loaded), share of ad revenue, monthly views needed to cover the loaded cost, 3-month coverage reserve.
tools.drive_notes: Math (assets/js/hiring-calculator.js): hourly → rate × hrs × 52/12; per_video → rate × units; monthly → retainer. Loaded cost = sticker × 1.15 (management, revisions, fees). Coverage views = loaded ÷ RPM band × 1000 (both band ends). The hiring rule: cover 3 months from revenue before signing.

tools.title: Repurposing Planner
tools.description: Turn one idea into a 5-platform mission-card checklist from the Phase 3 repurposing SOP.
tools.output: Five mission cards (YouTube Day 0, Short Day +1, TikTok Day +2, Reel Day +3, Facebook Day +4) each with a hook rewrite, atom test, and native-grammar checklist.
tools.drive_notes: Logic (assets/js/repurpose.js + assets/js/content-engine.js): atom test (does the insight survive standalone?), pillar prep (hook in first 15s), then the five staggered mission cards. Enforce native grammar — no watermarks, no copy-paste. 2.0 adds the full derivative map via ContentEngine.repurposeMap (7 derivatives: short clip, community reaction, TikTok cut, Reel cut, newsletter issue, X thread, Facebook post) — every derivative carries a required original element (repurposing is not re-uploading) plus the Oct-1 originality guardrails (ContentEngine.originalityGuardrails). Machine-readable map + guardrails: api/v1/content-engine.json repurposing_2_0 / originality_guardrails.

tools.title: Empire Simulator
tools.description: Simulate 12–24 months of channel growth + revenue — scenario library, A/B comparison, team hiring P&L — a model, not a prediction.

niche.description: Growth-model niche keys from the sim engine's nicheGrowth map.

monthly_growth_rate.description: Base monthly compounding growth at reference cadence (assumption, adjustable).

scenario_id.description: One-click preset: loads a full named starting config from the engine's SCENARIOS library (research-sourced assumptions).

horizon.description: 12 or 24 months. 24 adds year-2 diminishing returns: monthly growth decays x0.94/mo after month 12 (the engine's labeled curve).

type.description: First-Hire-guide role: editor, thumbnail designer, or virtual assistant.

monthly_cost_usd.description: Omit to use the guide preset: editor $1,400, thumbnail $120, VA $900.

hires.description: Team hires: each adds output/quality lift and subtracts monthly cost (month-by-month P&L: gross, team cost, net). First active month at 50% effect (ramp-up).

compare_with.description: A/B mode: {name_b, inputs_b} — compare(nameA, inputsA, nameB, inputsB, cfg) runs both over the same horizon and returns B-minus-A deltas plus a plain-language verdict.

name_b.description: Label for the B path (e.g. 'Tech reviewer').

inputs_b.description: Full SimulatorInput for the B path (or a scenario_id).

tools.output: 12- or 24-month projection: subs, views, and revenue per month per stream (ads, sponsors, affiliates, digital), month-by-month team P&L (gross, team cost, net), totals, milestones, and the full named-assumptions list. compare() adds side-by-side deltas (B minus A) and a verdict. exportPlan() renders the copy-my-empire-plan text. A model, not a prediction.
tools.drive_notes: Engine (assets/js/sim-engine.js, UMD — importable in node): simulate(inputs, cfg) with cfg = calculators.json. scenarioInputs(id) loads a named preset from the SCENARIOS library; compare(nameA, inputsA, nameB, inputsB, cfg) runs two configs over the same clock (deltas are B minus A); assumptionLines(inputs, res) is the always-visible assumptions panel; exportPlan(scenarioName, inputs, res) renders the share text. Growth compounds monthly x niche factor x quality x cadence (diminishing, capped 2.5x). Hires add output/quality and subtract cost monthly (first active month at 50% ramp). Year-2 decays growth x0.94/mo after month 12. RPMs come from calculators.json youtube_longform_rpm_bands. Every assumption is named in DEFAULTS and listed on-page.

tools.title: API Explorer
tools.description: Browse every api/v1 endpoint and preview JSON responses live in your browser — no key, no server.

input_schema.title: ApiExplorerInput
input_schema.description: No inputs — this tool is a read-only browser over the API itself.

tools.output: Live in-browser JSON previews of every endpoint, discovered from api/v1/index.json with a static fallback list.
tools.drive_notes: Discovery (assets/js/api-explorer.js): fetches api/v1/index.json, renders one GET button per endpoint record, pretty-prints responses. Agents can skip the UI and fetch the endpoints directly.

tools.title: Hook Builder
tools.description: Type your video topic, get five filmed-ready hooks — one per Short-Form Playbook structure. Flip-through cards.

topic.description: The video topic in one line (the payoff works best).

tools.output: Five filmed-ready hooks, one per Short-Form Playbook structure: open loop, cold start, contrarian take, numbered promise, question-as-hook.
tools.drive_notes: Logic (assets/js/hook-builder.js): topic → template fills per structure + the anti-hook checklist (no 'wait for it', no follow-begging, no channel-name cold open). The structures are craft formulas, not platform documentation.

tools.title: Idea Bank
tools.description: Capture ideas with hook-strength scores (1–5, Playbook structures), niche tags, and effort estimates — promote the best to production.

title.description: The idea in one line — the core of the video.

format.description: Long-form pillar, short-form post, or community text post.

niche.description: Niche tag — a Niche Atlas niche id from api/v1/niches.json (free text accepted).

effort.description: quick < 2h, afternoon = half day, week = full week build.

hook_score.description: Hook strength self-score against the five Short-Form Playbook structures (see api/v1/content-engine.json hook_structures).

tools.output: Banked ideas sorted by hook score (ties by FIFO), filterable by format, promotable to production (they deal into the content calendar). localStorage only.
tools.drive_notes: Logic (assets/js/content-engine.js, UMD — importable in node): hookScore(n) clamps 1–5; sortIdeas(ideas) sorts by hook score desc, ties by created asc, no mutation; filterIdeas(ideas, format) filters. Storage is the browser's localStorage (key cge_idea_bank_v1) — agents feed idea records directly to the engine functions.

tools.title: 90-Day Content Calendar
tools.description: Deal your idea bank into a 90-day grid: week-planner dealing rules, drag/keyboard moves, sponsor slots, copy-my-calendar export.

rest_day.description: 0=Mon … 6=Sun; non-negotiable rest — no placement, analytics review only.

ideas.description: Idea records (e.g. from the Idea Bank). Community ideas deal on the short cadence.

tools.output: 13-week grid: per-day long/short placements, open slots (never filler), backlog, midpoint-review flag on week 7. Export text + simulator input bridge + sponsor-slot marks.
tools.drive_notes: Logic (assets/js/content-engine.js, UMD — importable in node): dealIdeas(ideas, {longsPerWeek, shortsPerWeek, restDay, weeks}) — same dealing arithmetic as the 90-Day Planner: longs sort by hook score desc then round-robin across weeks onto non-rest work days; shorts deal every other work day; empty slots stay OPEN (never padded); surplus ideas return in unplaced; week 7 flagged midpointReview. exportCalendarText(deal) renders the copy-my-calendar text; simInputFromCadence(longs, shorts) returns {longform_per_week, shorts_per_week} for the Simulator; sponsored slots are calendar commitments only — price them in the Deal Room.

tools.title: Batching Planner
tools.description: Film-day math: does your shoot capacity actually cover your cadence? Honest surplus/shortfall, consistency-beats-volume framing.

videos_per_shoot_day.description: Long-form videos filmed per shoot day (honest average).

shoot_days_per_month.description: Scheduled, repeatable shoot days — 'I'll find the time' doesn't count.

tools.output: Required vs capacity per month (long + short), deltas, and a verdict: surplus (bank it), balanced (no slack), or shortfall (add a shoot day / drop a slot / merge formats).
tools.drive_notes: Logic (assets/js/content-engine.js, UMD — importable in node): batchingMath(opts) — capacity = shoot_days_per_month × videos_per_shoot_day; required = cadence × 52/12 (the honest month); verdict surplus/balanced/shortfall with guidance text. Pure arithmetic on the creator's own inputs — never a promise. Planning aid, not financial/legal/tax advice.

tools.title: The Money Map
tools.description: Find your stage on the $0-to-company journey: 7 questions, 5 stage playbooks, your next 3 moves. Stages are focus guides, never income promises.

revenue.description: Typical monthly content revenue band. The honest anchor: placement is driven by this, not by audience or team size.

bottleneck.description: Biggest bottleneck right now — selects the bottleneck-driven roadmap moves.

streams.description: Revenue streams actually paying right now.

tools.output: Stage placement (0–4: The Start Line / First $100 / The Engine Runs / The Business / The Company), sanity notes (audience-ahead, team-ahead), and a 3-move roadmap (stage signature move + 2 bottleneck-driven moves), the stage trap, and the graduate-when criteria. Placement anchored on the creator's own reported revenue band; stages are focus guides, never income promises.
tools.drive_notes: Logic (assets/js/money-map.js, UMD — importable in node): placeStage(a) — revenue band maps 0→0, 1-99→1, 100-999→2, 1k-9999→3, 10k-plus→4; if audience is 100k+ and base stage ≤ 2, stage+1 with an 'audience-ahead' note; employees with stage ≤ 2 adds a 'team-ahead' note. roadmap(a) — stage signature move (the stage's #1 tool) + two bottleneck-driven moves, deduped. STAGES carries the full playbook data (goal, 3 moves, trap, graduate). Planning aid, not financial/legal/tax advice.

tools.title: Diagnose My Video
tools.description: Pick your symptom — low CTR, the 30-second cliff, great retention but no subs — and get ranked causes with the fix from the chapter that owns it.

symptom.description: The symptom the creator sees in their analytics.

experience.description: Videos shipped. Under 50 = tuition phase: the data is thin, diagnose lightly.

tools.output: Ranked likely causes drawn from the site's chapters (Phase 1, Phase 2, Short-Form Playbook), each with chapter-grounded fixes and read-next links; the metric to watch next; context notes (tuition-phase caveat under 50 videos, swipe-feed completion-rate note for CTR on short-form). Thresholds labeled as creator-reported rules of thumb, never platform-published benchmarks.
tools.drive_notes: Engine (assets/js/video-doctor.js, UMD — importable in node): validInput(i) validates the three enums; diagnose(i) returns the symptom record with causes ranked 1..N (cause/why/fixes/links) plus notes. SYMPTOMS carries the full 8-symptom dataset. Diagnostic aid, not financial/legal/tax advice; never an income promise.
